intro.text: Warehouse Row stores the whole city's parcels on numbered shelves. Lately the basement floods and nobody knows why.
Quack. Every time someone asks for a shelf (malloc), someone must give it back (free). The water is what a memory leak looks like.

mid.text: The leaks are patched. Now the mail: every shelf has an address, and a pointer is just a note holding one.
Quack. *p means go to the address in p. Adding 1 to an int pointer steps one int, which is 4 bytes.

outro.text: Dry basement and parcels delivered. You can read memory now. Careful out there.
Quack. Next the Transit Hub, where we chain shelves together.

games.title: Stop the Flood
games.instructions: Follow the orders. malloc = click an empty shelf. free = click the shelf holding that crate. When orders end, free anything left over.

games.title: Special Delivery
games.instructions: Each shelf shows its address and the int stored there (4 bytes apiece). Click the shelf the pointer leads to.

rounds.hint: *p means the shelf AT the address in p.

rounds.prompt: p holds 0x108 and q = p + 1. Deliver to *q.
rounds.hint: p + 1 moves one int (4 bytes) forward.

rounds.prompt: p holds 0x100. After p += 3, deliver to *p.
p holds 0x114. After p--, deliver to *p.
rounds.hint: Subtracting 1 steps back one int (4 bytes).
